dialect.detail: Standard COBOL-85 style, likely compiled with GnuCOBOL or similar open-source compiler; uses LINE SEQUENTIAL organization and relative file paths typical of student/academic environments

purpose.domain_detail: Group project for course MAFD-4202, processing retail return transactions and generating a formatted report
purpose.summary: This program reads a returns transaction file (project1Return.out), processes each record to calculate tax owed at 13%, and writes a formatted report (project1R-Report.out) with transaction details, totals for records, transaction amounts, and tax owed. It is a student group project dated April 2018.

notable_features: ACCEPT FROM DATE / ACCEPT FROM TIME for timestamp in report header
COMPUTE with ROUNDED for tax calculation
PERFORM VARYING with dual UNTIL conditions (line count and EOF)
Formatted output using editing PIC clauses ($$,$$9.99, z9, 99b99b99b99)
Page break logic with line counter and page counter
WRITE ... AFTER ADVANCING PAGE for pagination
No COPY statements, no CALL statements, self-contained program
verdict.notes: Program is clearly a student group project (authors named, course code MAFD-4202 referenced in comments, dated 2018). Logic is straightforward and well-structured for a student exercise. Dialect is ambiguous between GnuCOBOL and other standard COBOL-85 compilers; LINE SEQUENTIAL and relative paths suggest a PC/GnuCOBOL environment.
